summary: The note explains how volunteers drive the success of community learning centers (CLCs), describing a surge in volunteer sign-ups since September 2023 and the impact of training programs and skilled volunteering. It reports statistics on satisfaction, learning outcomes, STEM engagement and the $18 million economic value of volunteer services. It also covers outreach for diverse volunteer bases and the future of volunteer engagement.
one_line: Volunteers, through training, skilled expertise and diverse outreach, have become the core driving force of community learning centers, with measurable educational and economic benefits.
key_facts: Since September 2023, urban areas and small communities have seen a substantial increase in volunteer participation at CLCs, sparked by a campaign from the Novel Futures Initiative.
The Novel Futures Initiative is a nonprofit aimed at empowering local education; its campaign highlighted the impact of volunteering on volunteers as well as students.
As of October 2023, the Educational Volunteer Network (EVN) reported a 25% increase in volunteer sign-up rates compared to the same period the previous year.
Jessica Miles, a retired teacher, volunteered at the Sunrise CLC in Elmont and became a role model for the volunteer movement.

The Brookstone CLC in Midville, led by Center Director Marcus Leung, launched a Volunteer Empowerment Program (VEP) in late September 2023 covering educational strategies, pedagogical tech and classroom management.
An EVN survey in November 2023 found centers with Empowerment Programs had a 40% increase in volunteer satisfaction and a 35% boost in learning outcomes for attendees.
The EVN survey noted that well-prepared volunteers tend to commit longer to their roles.
Computer engineer Raj Patel spent weekends at the Orchard Hill CLC teaching coding to teenagers as an example of skilled volunteering.
A CLC National Forum report from December 2023 showed a 50% increase in student participation in programs using skilled volunteering, particularly in STEM fields.
A January 2024 study by the Community Economic Development Association found volunteer contributions equal $18 million in educational services nationwide.
Volunteers often bring donated equipment or sponsored materials from workplaces or personal networks, extending CLC capabilities without prohibitive costs.
In 2024, CLCs are focusing on outreach to recruit volunteers from varied ethnic, cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds.
The Harmony CLC in Rivertown offers language classes led by volunteers proficient in the languages of its immigrant populations, improving their integration.
